items.stem: On the map, king minus man plus woman ends up closest to queen. What does this suggest about the word positions?

options.text: Man to king is the same step as woman to queen, so a relationship is a direction.
options.feedback: Nobody names the relationship. It appears because words used in similar ways get similar positions.

options.text: The model stores a definition of queen as a female king and looks it up.
options.feedback: The model stores positions, not definitions. The match comes from distances.

options.text: The model checks a list of royal titles and picks the matching one.
options.feedback: There is no list. Positions are learned from text, and in this demo they were placed by hand.

options.text: Queen was the only word left on the map after the others were removed.
options.feedback: Many words remain on the map. The result circle is nearest to queen.

items.stem: Before you try it: the option "Do not answer with the input words" is on for king minus man plus woman. What happens to the answer if you turn it off?

options.text: The nearest word becomes king, one of the input words.
options.feedback: The result point keeps most of the king position, so king is nearest. The well-known demonstration only works when the input words are excluded.

options.text: The answer stays queen, since queen is still nearest.
options.feedback: Queen is the nearest word only after king, man and woman are removed from the candidates.

options.text: The answer becomes man, since man is nearest to the result.
options.feedback: The result is built from king, so king is nearer to it than man is.

options.text: No word comes back, since all the candidates are removed.
options.feedback: The search always returns the nearest word. Without the exclusion it is king.

items.try: Turn the option off with king minus man plus woman selected and read the ranking.

items.stem: A vendor says its hiring tool is "only 3 percent biased" based on a word-analogy test. What is a reasonable response?

options.text: Ask how it was measured, since analogy tests can produce part of the result.
options.feedback: Embeddings reflect their corpus. The analogy method itself also adds to the result, so a single tidy number needs an explanation.

options.text: Accept the number, because it comes from a mathematical test.
options.feedback: A calculation can still measure the wrong thing. The method needs checking too.

options.text: Add an instruction to the prompt telling the model to ignore gender.
options.feedback: A prompt cannot remove the pattern, because it is built into the positions the model uses.

options.text: Conclude that the model has no bias, because it has no opinions.
options.feedback: Bias here comes from patterns in the text the model was built from, and it does not need opinions.

items.stem: Before you try it: the sentences "How do I sign up for a class?" and "How do I drop a class?" share five words. What will the similarity score be?

options.text: Low, because the two sentences mean opposite things.
options.feedback: The two arrows point in very different directions, so the cosine is low even though many words match.

options.text: High, because the two sentences share five words.
options.feedback: Counting shared words is what a keyword search does. The score here compares meaning.

options.text: Exactly 1, because the sentences are almost the same length.
options.feedback: Length does not matter. The score compares direction only.

options.text: Exactly 0, because the sentences are different.
options.feedback: The score drops toward 0 only when the arrows are at right angles. These are about 72 degrees apart.

items.try: Pick sentences A and C in the widget and read both numbers.

items.stem: A student asks how to avoid being charged twice for an enrollment. The best help page is titled "Idempotency keys". Why might a search by meaning still find it?

options.text: The question and the page have similar positions, even though they share no words.
options.feedback: This is retrieval: finding the text whose position is nearest to the question.

options.text: The search matches any page that contains the word charged.
options.feedback: That is keyword search. It would miss a page that does not contain the word.

options.text: The search reads every page in full each time to find the answer.
options.feedback: Retrieval compares positions, which is much cheaper than reading every page.

options.text: The page title is rewritten automatically to match the question.
options.feedback: Nothing is rewritten. The two texts are compared by position.
